**Uno – Quick‑Start Rules** | Section | What you need | How it works | |---------|---------------|--------------| | **Goal** | Be the first player to score 500 points (or whatever house rule you set). Points are earned by being the first to empty your hand in each round. | After each round, the winner tallies the total value of all cards left in opponents’ hands. That sum becomes the winner’s score for that round. | | **Deck** | 108 cards: 4 colors (Red, Yellow, Green, Blue) × 25 cards each + 8 Wild cards (4 + 4). | • 0–9 cards (one 0 per color, two of each 1–9).
• Action cards: Skip, Reverse, Draw Two (two of each per color).
• Wild cards: Wild (any color), Wild Draw Four (any color + force next player to draw 4). | | **Setup** | • Shuffle the deck.
• Deal 7 cards to each player.
• Place the remaining deck face‑down as the draw pile.
• Flip the top card of the draw pile to start the discard pile. If it’s an action card, apply its effect immediately (e.g., if it’s a Skip, the first player is skipped). | | **Turn Order** | Players sit in a circle. The first turn goes to the player left of the dealer (clockwise). Reverse cards change direction. | | **Playing a Card** | On your turn you may play **one** card that matches either the **color** or the **number/symbol** of the top discard.
• If you have no playable card, you must draw one from the draw pile.
• If the drawn card is playable, you may play it immediately; otherwise, your turn ends. | | **Special Cards** | • **Skip** – Next player loses their turn.
• **Reverse** – Reverses play direction. (In a 2‑player game, Reverse acts like Skip.)
• **Draw Two** – Next player draws two cards and loses their turn.
• **Wild** – You choose the new color.
• **Wild Draw Four** – You choose the new color; next player draws four cards and loses their turn.
**Wild Draw Four** can only be played if you have no other playable card of the current color. If challenged and you were wrong, you must draw 4 cards instead. | | **Calling “UNO”** | When you play your **second‑to‑last** card (i.e., you have one card left), you must shout “UNO!” before the next player takes their turn.
• If you forget and another player catches you, you must draw two penalty cards. | | **Winning a Round** | The round ends when a player discards their last card. That player is the round winner. | | **Scoring** | Add up the point values of all cards still in opponents’ hands:
• Number cards = face value.
• Skip, Reverse, Draw Two = 20 points each.
• Wild, Wild Draw Four = 50 points each.
Round winner’s score = sum of opponents’ points. | | **Game End** | First player to reach the target score (commonly 500) wins the game. | --- ### Quick Tips & Common Variations | Tip / Variation | Why it matters | |-----------------|----------------| | **Keep an eye on the discard pile** – Knowing what’s been played helps you anticipate opponents’ moves. | | **Use Wild Draw Four strategically** – Save it for when you’re about to run out of cards or when you need to block a strong opponent. | | **Challenge rule** – If you suspect a Wild Draw Four was played illegally, you can challenge. If you’re right, the offender draws 4; if wrong, you draw 4. | | **House rules** – Many groups add “Stacking” (draw two cards can be countered with another draw two) or “No Wild Draw Four unless you have no other playable card” (strict enforcement). | | **Speed play** – For a faster game, play until someone reaches 200 points or set a time limit. | Enjoy the colorful chaos of Uno!
